page: Amazon Web Services r7a.large is a memory-optimized instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. It features 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

The x86_64 architecture of the AMD EPYC processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic accelerators like AES and SHA_NI. Cache configuration consists of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 8 MB L3 cache per core.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25 percent. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth read performance are comparatively weaker, falling into the bottom 25 percent for tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, and large-block read operations. Write memory bandwidth and small-model LLM inference processing remain in the average tier.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong single-threaded execution, the r7a.large is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing or local disk storage. It is suitable for small-scale databases, caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
